sections.name: File setup, limiter
sections.title: Setup and per-address limit
sections.what: Brings in the image and response helpers, the lab service, the limiter and the colour helper, and allows 30 requests per address per minute.
sections.why: Likely reason: the image is generated on the server, so requests are limited to protect it.
sections.watch_out: The token in the address works as a password, so anyone with the link can see the card until sharing stops.

sections.name: GET
sections.title: Draw the Alter Ego card
sections.what: Looks up the card, returns not-found if it is missing, and draws the image with the label, evidence, display name, grade count and calibration in the brand colours.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond producing the share picture.
sections.watch_out: The image is publicly cached for an hour, so it can outlive a revocation for that long in outside caches.

summary: Draws the shareable Alter Ego card as a 1200 by 630 image for a valid share token, showing only the display name and the lead evidence.
purpose: Lets a fan share their Alter Ego result as a picture on social media.
why: The comment says the card is behind the fan's opt-in and can be revoked, and it shows no personal data beyond the display name.
how: 1) Limits requests per address to 30 per minute. 2) Looks up the card by the token in the address. 3) Returns not-found if the token is unknown or revoked. 4) Draws the image with the persona, evidence and grade counts, and returns it with a one-hour cache setting.
inputs: A GET with the token in the address. Card data comes from the lab service.
outputs: A 1200 by 630 image, or a JSON error for rate limits and not-found.
risks: The card is cached publicly for an hour, so a revoked link may still show for up to an hour in caches outside the app.
debug: If an image is blank or missing, check the card lookup in the lab service and the token. If an old image keeps showing, the public cache setting is the likely cause.
